analysis: Documentation-only change to docs/reference/configuration.md. The head side adds three table rows after base line 319 (head lines 320-323): DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP (exact `1`, default off), DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_DEPTH (1..3, default 1) and DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP_VERIFICATION. The patch excerpt is truncated at the VERIFICATION row, so its effect text was not seen. All three base units were reviewed as context and contain no changes. Security-relevant claims in the visible rows: the opt-in is off by default and read from the process environment. The first row says it is not forwarded to LaunchAgents and that DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP still disables it. The speculating owner refuses media, and an invalid depth fails the load rather than falling back. These are documentation claims about NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift (Setting.resolve), which was not supplied, so the behaviour is unverified. Relevant threat IDs are T-007 (output integrity: speculation is greedy and text-only), T-041 (prefix cache) and TB-007. Whether Super MTP changes prefix-cache save/restore, KV encryption or the SSD tier is not stated in the visible text, so it is an open question for the code pass. No changes to authorization, attestation, encryption, the wire protocol or billing are visible. The threat model needs no update from the visible rows. If the source pass for NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift shows the head's LOAD supplement bypasses memory admission or weight-hash verification, that would be a separate concern.
